title: Food systems & soil
examples: What is the difference between intensive and sustainable farming?
How does farming affect soil erosion?
Can we use farming to help the environment?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how we grow our food.
Intensive agriculture focuses on maximizing crop output quickly.
Sustainable agriculture aims to maintain soil health for the long term.
Erosion is the process where soil is moved away by wind or water.
Cover crops help prevent erosion by keeping roots in the soil.
In a real farm, planting diverse crops prevents soil from washing away.

faq.q: What is the biggest difference between the two farming styles?
faq.a: The main difference is that intensive farming prioritizes immediate high yields, while sustainable farming prioritizes long-term soil health.
asks: Which one is better for the planet?

faq.q: Does using chemicals always cause soil problems?
faq.a: Chemical overuse can reduce the natural life in the soil, making it less healthy over time.
asks: What happens if we use too many pesticides?

faq.a: Soil erosion is simply the wearing away and removal of topsoil by natural forces like running water or strong wind.
asks: Is erosion just dirt washing away?

faq.a: While not always mandatory, cover crops are a very effective way to keep soil protected between main harvests.
asks: Should I plant something when I'm not growing food?
What are cover crops used for?

faq.q: Does the size of the farm matter for sustainability?
faq.a: No, the practices used on the farm, like crop rotation, are more important than the total size of the land.
asks: Is it only big farms that can be sustainable?
Does farm size affect soil erosion?

facts: Sustainable farming methods aim to maintain soil structure and fertility.
Intensive farming often relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers and pesticides.
Erosion is accelerated when vegetation cover is removed from the soil surface.
Crop rotation involves planting different types of crops in sequence.

quiz.why: Crop rotation helps manage soil nutrients naturally and breaks pest cycles.

wrong.0: This depletes specific nutrients and attracts pests that thrive on one food source.
wrong.2: This compacts the soil, making it harder for roots to grow.
wrong.3: This can lead to nutrient runoff, polluting nearby water sources.

quiz.say: If a river flows over bare soil after a heavy storm, what process is most likely happening?
quiz.why: The force of the running water physically carries away the topsoil particles.

wrong.0: Leaching is when water dissolves nutrients deep underground, not necessarily moving soil.
wrong.1: Compaction is the process of squeezing air out of the soil, not moving it away.
wrong.2: This describes a chemical reaction, not the physical removal of soil by water.

quiz.say: A farmer plants beans, then corn, then oats in the same field over three years. This is an example of:
quiz.why: This planned sequence of different crops is the definition of crop rotation.

wrong.0: Remediation is fixing pollution, not just changing the crop sequence.
wrong.2: Monocropping means planting only one type of crop repeatedly.
wrong.3: This describes a high-input method, not the pattern of planting.
